obs: "The known rule being, that a statute for the commencement of which no time is fixed, commences from its date"
"This is clearly so, unless some provision is found in the act of admission postponing the time when it shall take effect"
"The act becomes effectual upon the day of its date. In such cases it is operative from the first moment of that day. Fractions of the day are not recognized."
"There is no statute fixing the time when acts of Congress shall take effect, but it is settled that where no other time is prescribed they take effect from their date."

"We do not see how there can be any doubt that this repealing section went into immediate effect. The law itself went into immediate effect, although, it is true, various provisions of it, contained in other sections, were postponed to take effect"
Mr. Chief Justice Marshall remarked that it was the known rule "that a statute for the commencement of which no time is fixed, commences from its date;"

"The Supreme Court also concluded that as the amendment named no date when it was to take effect it would become effective some two months later, on September 1, 1939, as provided by 4 of the Statutory Construction Act of May 28, 1937"
"Nor does anything we can discern about Congress' purpose in enacting 1002 rebut the presumption that it became effective at once."
"(applying the rule in Arnold v. United States ... that statutes become effective immediately)"
United States v. R. L. C.
“applying the rule in Arnold v. United States… that statutes become effective immediately”
"The omission simply remits us to the general rule that when a statute has no effective date, absent a clear direction by Congress to the contrary, [it] takes effect on the date of its enactment."
